# dsh-codex-bridge
A DeepSeek Harness bundle that lets the agent read the local **Codex CLI** quota and delegate hard t
asks to `codex exec` with a model and reasoning effort that fit the current ChatGPT-plan budget.
It is a host-only DSH plugin: two tools, no browser half, no build step, and no npm dependencies.
> Unofficial community plugin. Not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI, Codex, or DeepSeek.
## What it adds
| Tool | What it does | Codex usage |
| `codex_status` | Reads the 5-hour and weekly ChatGPT-plan windows, reset times, credits, the model

ladder, and the quota-aware recommendation. | none |
| `codex_delegate` | Runs one non-interactive
`codex exec` task in a chosen directory and returns the answer, token usage, thread id, and the quot
a left afterwards. | yes |
`codex_status` talks to `codex app-server` (`account/rateLimits/read`, `model/list`). `codex_delegat
e` is the only path that spends model usage.
## Quota policy
The deployment default is intentionally narrow:

- **Default:** `gpt-6.1-sol` at reasoning effort **`high`**.
- **Reserve:** when either window has *

*10% or less left**, auto switches to `gpt-5.6-sol` at `medium`.
- **`gpt-6-astra`:** never selected
automatically. An explicit `model: "gpt-6-astra"` is refused unless the caller also sets `allow_exp

ensive_model: true`, because it consumes the shared quota much faster.
- **Floors:** the model never

goes below `gpt-5.6-sol`; reasoning effort never goes below `medium`.
- **Blocked:** at 95% used, o
r when the backend disallows ordinary usage, runs are refused unless `allow_low_quota: true`.
Recommendation table (`model=auto`, `reasoning_effort=auto`):
| Complexity | Normal (both windows > 10% left) | Reserve (either window ≤ 10% left) |

| `simple` | `gpt-6.1-sol` / `high` | `gpt-5.6-sol` / `medium` |
| `standard` | `gpt-6.1-sol` / `hig

h` | `gpt-5.6-sol` / `medium` |
| `hard` | `gpt-6.1-sol` / `high` | `gpt-5.6-sol` / `medium` |
| `cr
itical` | `gpt-6.1-sol` / `high` | `gpt-5.6-sol` / `high` |
Explicit choices are validated, never silently downgraded. A refusal names the selectable models or
e validated, never silently downgraded. A refusal names the selectable models or the missing opt-in.
### About `gpt-6.1-sol`
The installed Codex CLI build may not list `gpt-6.1-sol` in `model/list` even though the backend acc
epts it (a real `codex exec` run confirmed this during development). `codex_status` therefore shows
it as a **configured** model and warns that `codex exec` may print a missing-model-metadata warning.
Change `defaultModel` / `minModel` in the config if your Codex account uses different ids.

## Usage
Ask the agent:
> Check the Codex quota, then delegate this hard problem to Codex with the right model and effort.
The agent calls `codex_status`, picks a complexity (or passes explicit `model` / `reasoning_effort`)
, then calls `codex_delegate`. The task must be self-contained: Codex cannot see the DSH conversatio
n, so include absolute paths, symptoms, constraints, and the exact deliverable.
Default sandbox is `read-only`. Pass `sandbox: "workspace-write"` and a `cwd` only when Codex must e
ndbox is `read-only`. Pass `sandbox: "workspace-write"` and a `cwd` only when Codex must edit files.

## Limitations
- The app-server methods belong to the installed Codex CLI version; an incompatible upgrade fails wi

th `CODEX_RPC` / `CODEX_PROTOCOL` instead of inventing data.
- Codex does not share this conversatio

n's context.
- Default `read-only` means Codex can read `cwd` but cannot write; `workspace-write` ke

eps writes under `cwd` and still follows Codex's own sandbox/network policy.
- The returned quota is

a percentage snapshot, not an exact token reservation; the tiers are spend guardrails.
- `gpt-6.1-s
ol` availability and model metadata depend on the Codex CLI build and account; configure other ids i
ability and model metadata depend on the Codex CLI build and account; configure other ids if needed.
